transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hello. The things that used to mean everything to me—my garden, my quilts, my walks—don’t matter anymore, and I can’t make myself care about any of it. Ever since my sister passed away, I just feel like I've lost all interest in the world.
I am so sorry for your loss. Could you tell me when your sister passed away, and how long you have been feeling this way?

Thank you, that is very kind of you to say. My sister passed away unexpectedly about a year and five months ago, and I started feeling this heavy, joyless way a few months after her funeral. It has been going on almost constantly now for well over a year.
Along with this loss of interest, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels over this past year?

I've pretty much stopped wanting to eat because food just tastes like cardboard, and I have to force myself to swallow a few bites of toast or soup. I also feel completely exhausted from the moment I wake up, and even simple things like showering or walking to the mailbox wear me out so much that I have to sit down and rest.
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, perhaps blaming yourself for things related to your sister's passing or other areas of your life?

Yes, I constantly feel like a terrible, useless person who has failed my sister and my whole family. I keep replaying tiny mistakes I made years ago, and I've become convinced that her unexpected death and everything else that has gone wrong is entirely my fault and that I deserve to suffer.
During this incredibly difficult time, have you had any thoughts of ending your life, or felt that you would be better off dead?

Yes, almost every day I catch myself thinking it would be better if I just didn't wake up. I've even pictured taking all my old pain pills at once so I could stop being a burden to everyone, though that thought really scares me afterward.

Have you ever experienced a similar period of deep sadness, exhaustion, or loss of interest at any other point in your life before your sister passed away? Or is this the very first time you have ever felt this way?
No, this is the very first time I have ever felt this way in my life. Before my sister passed away, I was always so active, lively, and involved in my church and community.

Sometimes when people are going through such a painful time, they might hear voices or see things that others don't, or hold beliefs that others tell them aren't real. Have you experienced anything like that?

Yes, actually... at night when the house is quiet, I often hear my sister calling my name from the hallway and telling me I'm a burden and should just come with her. I've also become convinced that some of the ladies from my church are working with the hospital and the city to watch me and take my house away, even though my daughter insists it isn't real.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with her first episode of severe depression, characterized by marked anhedonia, severe fatigue, significant appetite loss, profound guilt, and suicidal ideation, lasting for over a year following her sister's death. The episode is accompanied by psychotic features, including auditory hallucinations (hearing her deceased sister's voice telling her she is a burden) and persecutory delusions (believing church members and the hospital are plotting to take her house). This clinical picture aligns with a Severe Depressive Episode with Psychotic Symptoms (F32.3).
